Subject: Re: comparison of Affymetrix data from cartridge and HT arrays

Hi Elizabeth,

As Paul mentioned, we are trying to extract something akin to gene
expression data from the exon CEL files. I think we have distilled this
down to two key issues:

1. An exception thrown when attempting to execute fit(plm, ...) -- Error
report claims that the gene-centric CDF file and exon CEL files are
incompatible. I have appended the details of the error message.

2. Converting transcript clusters to genes -- Ju explained that the
function getChipEffects() outputs expression levels organized by
transcript clusters, not gene symbols. He wonders whether you or Mark
Robinson have another function that estimates gene expression based on
the transcript-cluster expression data. If so, could you direct me to
that function?

Here is additional information, in case anything else looks out of place:

----------------------------------------------

We are using the gene-centric CDF file:

HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy.cdf

which is located on aurora in directory:


/home/wjgibb/data/breast/cell/exon/annotationData/chipTypes/HuEx-1_0-st-v2

I downloaded the gene-centric CDF from:


http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/ensembl-gene-defintions

We are currently running R version 2.6.0 on aurora. The AROMA script is
attached.

Re item 1 above, the error report is appended. The same error occurs
when attempting to execute plotNuse(), plotRle() and getChipEffects().

In spite of the exceptions thrown, fit(plm, ...) appears to run to
completion, and the script writes expression data (?) to file:

/home/wjgibb/data/breast/cell/exon/bcgc_gene_norm.txt

Expression is zero for many of the transcript cluster IDs in the txt file.

Other things we tried: Testing the AROMA script on the usual
exon-centric CDF file -- works fine; no exceptions thrown. Surprisingly,
the expression data calculated using the exon-centric CDF file is
identical to the expression data calculated using the gene-centric CDF
file (I diff'd the respective .txt files returned by getChipEffects()).

------------------------------------------------------

Many thanks.

Bill

------------------------------------------------------

>>>>>>>> Hello Elizabeth,
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> I am working on a gene expression project with Paul Spellman.
>>>>>>>> The project involves comparing gene expression data acquired
>>>>>>>> from two different Affymetrix platforms -- both have U-133A
>>>>>>>> probe sets, however one platform is the regular cartridge
>>>>>>>> array, whereas the other platform is the high-throughput array
>>>>>>>> (HTA). In comparing the two data sets, I've noticed some
>>>>>>>> interesting patterns. After discussing the findings with Paul,
>>>>>>>> he suggested that I contact you to see whether you could take a
>>>>>>>> look at the results and perhaps critique the (simple) method
>>>>>>>> that I used to map expression values from 'cartridge-space' to
>>>>>>>> 'HTA-space.' I am wondering whether a probe-level model or
>>>>>>>> perhaps a (post-RMA) gene-level model might be a more
>>>>>>>> appropriate way to link the two data sets (e.g. encoding a
>>>>>>>> platform-effect). Would you be willing to take a look? If so,
>>>>>>>> could you suggest a time that is convenient for you? I work in
>>>>>>>> the Potter St bldg, however it is no problem for me to come up
>>>>>>>> to the campus.
